newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF looks for stronger earnings, sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: BASF looks for stronger earnings, sales in 1997.

text.p: German chemicals giant BASF AG on Tuesday said it expects to post stronger 1997 earnings and an increase in sales, benefiting from the global economic recovery.
"We are looking for further volume increases and stable to slightly better prices, this improves the prospects for 1997," the group said in a statement.
Sales this year are expected to top 49 billion marks after jumping 5.5 percent to 48.77 billion marks in 1996 when pre-tax profit climbed 6.9 percent to 4.4 billion marks, the group said.

BASF, the last of Germany's three chemical giants to report its 1996 results, said 1997 has gotten off to a strong start as incoming orders as well as orders on hand have risen in the first few months of this year compared with the end of 1996.

"We plan further growth with a portfolio that is strengthened through further disinvestments and acquisitions," BASF said. Investments are expected to be increased to 3.8 billion marks this year from 3.6 billion marks in 1996.
BASF also said it expects stronger domestic demand, marking an improvement from sluggish economic conditions in Germany which kept a lid on domestic sales last year.
While total group sales climbed 5.5 percent, they climbed only 2.8 percent to 12.97 billion marks in Germany.
BASF, which is long known for its very conservative earnings forecasts and opaque hints about future plans, will hold a news conference later today.
In March BASF's rivals Hoechst AG and Bayer AG disappointed the markets with weak fourth quarter earnings and a subdued outlook which sent chemical industry shares into a tailspin.

Analysts at that time said however that BASF, which was also sucked into the share market's losses, presented the strongest figures, boasting a 21.4 percent rise in its 1996 dividend payout to 1.70 marks.
